title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञविभागयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 13: The Field and the Knower of the Field

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)

sentences.t:
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
sentences.tr:
idam śarīram kaunteya kṣetram iti abhidhīyate |
etat yaḥ vetti tam prāhuḥ kṣetrajñaḥ iti tad-vidaḥ ||

morph.gloss: this (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with śarīram)
to call, name (abhidhīyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is called'; kṣetram+iti simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel; iti+abhidhīyate → ity abhidhīyate, -i+a-→-y a-)
this (etat: nom./acc. sg. neut., referring to śarīram; -t+y-→-d y-)
that, him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of prāhuḥ)
to declare, call (prāhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. 'they call')

knowing, knower (from jñā, second compound member; kṣetra-jña: 'the knower of the field', nom. sg. masc., a quoted predicate name kept in the nominative though logically the object of prāhuḥ, an iti-quotation idiom; visarga elided before the following vowel i-)
to know (vid-, 'knower', second compound member; tad-vidaḥ: 'the knowers of that [truth]', nom. pl. masc., subject of prāhuḥ)

sentences.l: This body, son-of-Kuntī, is-called the-field; who this knows, him the-knowers-of-that call the-knower-of-the-field.
sentences.i: This body, Kaunteya, is called the field; and the one who knows it is called, by those who know, the knower of the field.
sentences.n: The chapter opens with no question from Arjuna — Kṛṣṇa continues speaking unprompted, straight from chapter 12's close — and announces its two key terms at once, both translated per this pipeline's convention rather than left in Sanskrit: kṣetra, 'the field' (the body and its whole apparatus), and kṣetrajña, 'the knower of the field' (the conscious self that inhabits it). The construction is relative-correlative (yaḥ ... tam, 'who ... him'), and the closing kṣetrajñaḥ iti prāhuḥ, 'they call [him] "kṣetrajñaḥ"', keeps the quoted name in the nominative even though tam, its logical antecedent, is accusative — a standard idiom where an iti-quotation retains the form it would have as an independent statement. Sandhi: etad yo is etat+yaḥ (-t+y-→-d y-, then -aḥ+v-→-o); kṣetram ity abhidhīyate packs kṣetram+iti (simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel) and iti+abhidhīyate (-i+a-→-y a-); kṣetrajña iti shows the visarga of kṣetrajñaḥ eliding before the following vowel i- (a non-a vowel, unlike the -o'-pattern reserved for a following short a-).

sentences.t:
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥
sentences.tr:
kṣetra-jñam ca api mām viddhi sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata |
kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ jñānam yat tat jñānam matam mama ||

morph.gloss: knowing, knower (second compound member; kṣetra-jña: 'the knower of the field', acc. sg. masc., predicate complement of mām with viddhi: 'know me [as]…')
I (mām: acc. sg., object of viddhi)
the field (sarva-kṣetra: loc. pl. 'in all fields')
the knower of the field (kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ: gen. dual 'of the field and its knower'; -oḥ+j-→-or j-)
which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative; simply written joined with the following tat, both ending in -t)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut. correlative; -t+j-→-j j-)
to think, hold to be (mata: past participle 'considered, held', nom. sg. neut.)
I (mama: gen. sg. 'by me, in my view')

sentences.l: The-knower-of-the-field, and-also, me know, in-all-fields, O descendant-of-Bharata; of-the-field-and-its-knower the-knowledge which — that [is] knowledge, held [by] me.
sentences.i: Know me also, Bhārata, to be the knower of the field in every field; the knowledge of the field and its knower — that, I hold, is true knowledge.
sentences.n: A programmatic identification: Kṛṣṇa is the kṣetrajña present in every kṣetra, and knowledge of the kṣetra-kṣetrajña distinction is itself defined as jñāna, real knowledge — the theme this chapter works out through verse 18. Yat tat jñānam, 'the knowledge which — that [is] knowledge', doubles the relative and correlative purely for emphasis, meaning simply 'that is [true] knowledge'; the same device recurs at verse 12. Sandhi: cāpi is ca+api (a+a→ā); kṣetrakṣetrajñayor jñānaṃ is kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ+jñānam (-oḥ+j-→-or j-, the dual genitive's visarga becoming r before a voiced consonant); yattajjñānaṃ packs yat+tat (simply written together, both ending in -t) + tat+jñānam (-t+j-→-j j-).

sentences.t:
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥
sentences.tr:
tat kṣetram yat ca yādṛk ca yat vikāri yataḥ ca yat |
sa ca yaḥ yat-prabhāvaḥ ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu ||

morph.gloss: that (tat: acc. sg. neut., anticipating the description to follow)
the field (acc. sg. neut., object of śṛṇu)
which (yat: nom./acc. sg. neut. relative; -t+c-→-c c-)
of what kind, what sort (yādṛk: nom. sg. neut., the stem-final -ś appearing as -k word-finally)
which, what (yat: nom./acc. sg. neut. relative; -t+v-→-d v-)
possessing what modification, subject to what change (nom. sg. neut.)
from what, whence (yataḥ: ablative adverb; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
what (nom. sg. neut. relative, 'and what [it is]')
he (sa: nom. sg. masc., referring to the knower of the field; the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant)
power, might (yat-prabhāva: 'he whose power is what', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of śṛṇu, summing up the preceding description)
a summary, compendium (samāsena: instr. sg. used adverbially, 'in brief')
I (me: enclitic gen. sg., 'from me' with śṛṇu)

sentences.l: That field — which, and of-what-kind, and what-its-modifications, and from-what, and what; and he who, and of-what-power — that, in-brief, from-me hear.
sentences.i: Hear from me, in brief, what that field is, of what kind, what changes it undergoes, and from what it arises; and who he is, and what power he has.
sentences.n: A programmatic verse announcing the topics to follow: five relative questions about the field (what it is, its qualities, its transformations, its source — verses 5-6's twenty-four-fold analysis) and two about its knower (who he is, what power he has — taken up from verse 19 on), all gathered under tat samāsena me śṛṇu, 'hear that from me in brief', the imperative governing the rest of the chapter. Grammar: a chain of relative pronouns (yat, yādṛk, yad-vikāri, yataḥ, yat, yaḥ, yat-prabhāvaḥ) each introducing an indirect question, with no main clause until the final śṛṇu. Sa, the irregular sandhi form of the pronoun saḥ before any following consonant (never -o or -aḥ there, an exception specific to this word), appears here for the first time in this chapter and recurs at verses 23, 27 and 29. Sandhi: yac ca is yat+ca (-t+c-→-c c-); yataś ca is yataḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); yad vikāri is yat+vikāri (-t+v-→-d v-, voicing before a voiced consonant); yo is yaḥ, -aḥ before y-→-o; yat-prabhāvaś ca is yat-prabhāvaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-).

sentences.t:
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् ।
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥
sentences.tr:
ṛṣibhiḥ bahudhā gītam chandobhiḥ vividhaiḥ pṛthak |
brahma-sūtra-padaiḥ ca eva hetumadbhiḥ viniścitaiḥ ||

morph.gloss: sage, seer (ṛṣibhiḥ: instr. pl. 'by the sages'; -iḥ+b-→-ir b-)
to sing (gīta: past participle 'sung', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
[Vedic] meter, hymn (chandobhiḥ: instr. pl. 'in meters'; -iḥ+v-→-ir v-)
brahman, the absolute (kept untranslated per convention; first compound member)
word, expression (brahma-sūtra-pada: 'the words of the Brahma-sūtra', instr. pl.; -aiḥ+c-→-aiś c-)
reasoned, endowed with logical grounds (hetumadbhiḥ: instr. pl., agreeing with padaiḥ; -iḥ+v-→-ir v-)
to determine, ascertain (viniścita: past participle 'well-ascertained, definitively established', instr. pl.)

sentences.l: By-the-sages, in-many-ways, [it is] sung, in-various meters, separately; in-the-words-of-the-Brahma-sūtra too, indeed — reasoned, well-ascertained.
sentences.i: It has been sung by the sages in many ways, separately in various meters, and also in the reasoned, well-established aphorisms of the Brahma-sūtra.
sentences.n: This continues verse 3's sentence without its own finite verb, appealing to the authority of prior tradition before Kṛṣṇa gives his own account from verse 5: the teaching has been gītam, 'sung', by sages in various Vedic chandas, and set out hetumadbhiḥ viniścitaiḥ, 'reasoned and definitively established', in brahma-sūtra-padaiḥ, the aphorisms of the Brahma-sūtra (Bādarāyaṇa's Vedānta-sūtra, or Upaniṣadic aphorisms on brahman more generally). Sandhi: ṛṣibhir bahudhā and chandobhir vividhaiḥ both show -iḥ+voiced consonant→-ir; padaiś caiva packs padaiḥ+ca (-aiḥ+c-→-aiś c-) + ca+eva (a+e→ai); hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ shows the same -iḥ+v-→-ir v- pattern once more.

sentences.t:
महाभूतान्यहंकारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च ।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥
sentences.tr:
mahā-bhūtāni ahaṃkāraḥ buddhiḥ avyaktam eva ca |
indriyāṇi daśa-ekam ca pañca ca indriya-gocarāḥ ||

morph.gloss: the great elements (mahā-bhūtāni: nom. pl. neut.; -āni+a-→-āny a-)
the ego, the 'I-maker' (nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before b-→-o)
one (daśa-eka: 'ten-and-one, eleven', nom. sg. neut., used appositively with indriyāṇi: the ten organs of perception and action plus manas, the mind)
range, domain, object (indriya-gocara: 'the objects of the senses', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: The-great-elements, the-ego, the-intellect, and the-unmanifest indeed, and the-senses ten-and-one, and five, and the-objects-of-the-senses:
sentences.i: The five great elements, the ego, the intellect, and the unmanifest; the eleven senses; and the five objects of the senses:
sentences.n: This opens Kṛṣṇa's own twenty-four-fold Sāṃkhya-style analysis of the field (continued in verse 6), listing without a finite verb: the five mahā-bhūtāni (earth, water, fire, air, space), ahaṃkāra (the ego, the 'I-maker'), buddhi (the intellect), avyaktam (the unmanifest, i.e. nature prior to its evolutes), the eleven indriyas (five organs of perception, five of action, and manas, the mind, counted together as daśa-ekam, 'ten and one'), and the pañca indriya-gocarāḥ, the five sense-objects (sound, touch, form, taste, smell) — twenty-four items complete by the end of this verse (5+1+1+1+11+5), the classical Sāṃkhya tally of tattvas apart from puruṣa; verse 6 adds not further items but the field's modifications (vikāra). Sandhi: mahābhūtāny ahaṃkāro packs mahā-bhūtāni+ahaṃkāraḥ (-āni+a-→-āny a-) and ahaṃkāraḥ+buddhiḥ (-aḥ before b-→-o); buddhir avyaktam eva shows -iḥ+a-→-ir a-; daśaikaṃ is daśa+ekam (a+e→ai); cendriyagocarāḥ is ca+indriya-gocarāḥ (a+i→e).

sentences.t:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः ।
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
icchā dveṣaḥ sukham duḥkham saṃghātaḥ cetanā dhṛtiḥ |
etat kṣetram samāsena sa-vikāram udāhṛtam ||

morph.gloss: the aggregate, the composite [body] (nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
a summary, compendium (samāsena: instr. sg. used adverbially, 'in brief')
modification, transformation (sa-vikāram: 'together with its modifications', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to declare, state (udāhṛta: past participle 'declared', nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)

sentences.l: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the-aggregate, awareness, firmness — this [is] the-field, in-brief, together-with-its-modifications, declared.
sentences.i: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the bodily aggregate, awareness, and steadfastness — this, in brief, together with its modifications, is what is called the field.
sentences.n: This completes the twenty-four-fold analysis begun in verse 5 (five elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, eleven senses, five sense-objects) by naming its further modifications (vikāra): icchā (desire), dveṣa (aversion), sukha and duḥkha (pleasure and pain), saṃghāta (the aggregate, i.e. the body as a composite whole), cetanā (awareness) and dhṛti (firmness) — the whole of verses 5-6 closed by etat kṣetraṃ samāsena savikāram udāhṛtam, 'this is the field, declared in brief, together with its modifications'. Sandhi: saṃghātaś cetanā is saṃghātaḥ+cetanā (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); savikāram udāhṛtam is simply written joined (-m before u- unaffected).

sentences.t:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् ।
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥
sentences.tr:
amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṃsā kṣāntiḥ ārjavam |
ācārya-upāsanam śaucam sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ ||

morph.gloss: freedom from pride, absence of self-conceit (nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined with the following word, -m unaffected before the vowel)
freedom from hypocrisy, absence of ostentation (nom. sg. neut.; likewise joined)
attendance upon, reverence (ācārya-upāsana: 'reverence for the teacher', nom. sg. neut.)
steadiness, stability (nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to restrain, control (vinigraha: 'restraint, control', ātma-vinigraha: 'self-restraint', nom. sg. masc.)

sentences.l: Absence-of-pride, absence-of-hypocrisy, non-violence, patience, uprightness; service-to-the-teacher, purity, steadiness, self-restraint;
sentences.i: Freedom from pride and hypocrisy, non-violence, patience, uprightness; reverence for one's teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control;
sentences.n: This opens the virtue-list running through verse 11, all in apposition as the subject of etaj jñānam iti proktam, 'this is declared to be knowledge' (verse 11) — twenty abstract qualities defining jñāna not as doctrine but as a way of living. Amānitva and adambhitva, 'freedom from pride' and 'from hypocrisy/ostentation', set the list's tone: humility before any positive achievement. Ācārya-upāsanam, 'reverence for the teacher', reflects the traditional guru-centered transmission of this knowledge. Sandhi: kṣāntir ārjavam is kṣāntiḥ+ārjavam (-iḥ+ā-→-ir ā-); ācāryopāsanaṃ is ācārya+upāsanam (-a+u-→-o-); the neuter nouns amānitvam and adambhitvam are simply written joined with what follows, the final -m unaffected before each following vowel.

sentences.t:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहंकार एव च ।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥
sentences.tr:
indriya-artheṣu vairāgyam anahaṃkāraḥ eva ca |
janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam ||

morph.gloss: dispassion, non-attachment (nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
freedom from egoism (nom. sg. masc.; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)

repeated seeing, constant contemplation (janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam: 'the repeated contemplation of the evil inherent in birth, death, old age, sickness, [and] suffering', nom. sg. neut.; doṣa+anudarśana→doṣānudarśana, -a+a-→-ā-)

sentences.l: Dispassion toward-sense-objects, and-absence-of-egoism too, and; of-birth-death-old-age-disease-suffering, the-repeated-contemplation-of-the-fault.
sentences.i: Dispassion toward sense-objects, and freedom from egoism as well, and a constant awareness of the fault inherent in birth, death, old age, sickness and suffering;
sentences.n: The virtue-list continues: vairāgyam, 'dispassion', toward indriya-arthāḥ, sense-objects, and an-ahaṃkāra, freedom from egoism — the same pairing already made at 12.13's nirmama/nirahaṃkāra. The whole second line is one compound, janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam, 'the repeated contemplation of the fault inherent in birth, death, old age, sickness, [and] suffering' — a standing formula for the reflection that turns the mind toward renunciation. Sandhi: indriyārtheṣu is indriya+artheṣu (-a+a-→-ā-); anahaṃkāra eva shows the visarga dropping before the following vowel e- (a non-a vowel); within the closing compound, duḥkha-doṣānudarśanam packs doṣa+anudarśanam (-a+a-→-ā-).

sentences.t:
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ।
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥
sentences.tr:
asaktiḥ anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu |
nityam ca sama-cittatvam iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapattiṣu ||

morph.gloss: freedom from clinging, absence of fondness (nom. sg. masc., from abhi-ṣvañj 'to embrace, cling to')
and so on, et cetera (putra-dāra-gṛha-ādi: 'son, wife, house, and the like', loc. pl.)
the state of mind, disposition (sama-cittatva: 'evenness of mind', nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
occurrence, happening (iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapatti: 'the occurrence of the welcome and the unwelcome', loc. pl.)

sentences.l: Non-attachment, absence-of-clinging, toward-son-wife-house-and-so-on; constant, and evenness-of-mind toward-the-occurrence-of-the-desired-and-undesired.
sentences.i: Non-attachment and freedom from clinging to son, wife, home and the like; an even mind, always, toward whatever comes, welcome or unwelcome —
sentences.n: The list continues with detachment from family and possessions (putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu, 'toward son, wife, house, and so on' — dāra, properly plural in form, is the standard word for 'wife') and sama-cittatvam, 'evenness of mind', maintained nityam, 'constantly', toward iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapattiṣu, 'whatever occurs, welcome or unwelcome' — the same equanimity toward opposite pairs central to 12.18's samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca. Sandhi: asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ is asaktiḥ+anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-); gṛhādiṣu is gṛha+ādiṣu (-a+ā-→-ā-); the closing compound packs iṣṭa+aniṣṭa (-a+a-→-ā-) and aniṣṭa+upapattiṣu (-a+u-→-o-).

sentences.t:
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥
sentences.tr:
mayi ca ananya-yogena bhaktiḥ avyabhicāriṇī |
vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratiḥ jana-saṃsadi ||

morph.gloss: undivided, having no other [object] (first compound member)
unwavering, not deviating (nom. sg. fem., agreeing with bhaktiḥ)
secluded, solitary (vivikta: past participle, first compound member)
the habit of resorting to, frequenting (vivikta-deśa-sevitva: 'the habit of resorting to secluded places', nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
assembly, crowd (jana-saṃsad: 'the assembly of people', loc. sg.)

sentences.l: Toward-me, and-by-undivided-yoga, unwavering devotion; the-habit-of-resorting-to-secluded-places, distaste-for-the-assembly-of-people.
sentences.i: Unwavering devotion toward me through undivided yoga; a preference for solitary places, a distaste for the company of crowds;
sentences.n: This introduces bhakti explicitly into the virtue-list (translated throughout, as since chapters 7 and 9, as 'devotion'), qualified as avyabhicāriṇī, 'unwavering, unswerving', and practiced ananya-yogena, 'through undivided yoga' — the same singleness of devotion insisted on at 12.6's ananyena eva yogena. Vivikta-deśa-sevitvam and arati janasaṃsadi, 'frequenting solitary places' and 'distaste for crowds', describe the outward, ascetic complement to this inward devotion. Sandhi: cānanyayogena is ca+ananya-yogena (a+a→ā); bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī is bhaktiḥ+avyabhicāriṇī (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-); aratir jana- is aratiḥ+jana- (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-).

sentences.t:
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् ।
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥
sentences.tr:
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam |
etat jñānam iti proktam ajñānam yat ataḥ anyathā ||

morph.gloss: relating to the self, the spiritual (first compound member)
constancy (adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva: 'constancy in knowledge of the self', nom. sg. neut.)
the true nature, reality (first compound member)
seeing, insight (tattva-jñāna-artha-darśana: 'insight into the aim/purpose of the knowledge of reality', nom. sg. neut.)
to declare, proclaim (prokta: past participle 'declared', nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined with the following word, -m unaffected before the vowel)
ignorance (nom. sg. neut., subject of the next clause)
what, whatever (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative; -t+a-→-d a-)
from this, than this (ataḥ: ablative of comparison; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)

sentences.l: Constancy-in-knowledge-of-the-self, insight-into-the-purpose-of-the-knowledge-of-truth — this [is] declared [to be] knowledge; ignorance [is] what [is] other than this.
sentences.i: Constancy in spiritual knowledge, and insight into the purpose of the knowledge of the ultimate reality — this is declared to be knowledge; whatever is other than this is ignorance.
sentences.n: This closes the virtue-list of verses 7-11 with its summary verdict: etaj jñānam iti proktam, 'this is declared to be knowledge' — meaning the whole preceding catalog of qualities, not any body of doctrine — while ajñānam yat ataḥ anyathā, 'ignorance is whatever differs from this', dismisses every rival claimant to the name. Adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam, 'constancy in knowledge of the self', and tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam, 'insight into the purpose of the knowledge of reality' (keeping liberation, not mere erudition, as the aim), are the list's final two items. Sandhi: etaj jñānam iti is etat+jñānam (-t+j-→-j j-); yad ataḥ is yat+ataḥ (-t+a-→-d a-, voicing before a vowel); ato'nyathā is ataḥ+anyathā (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते ।
अनादि मत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
jñeyam yat tat pravakṣyāmi yat jñātvā amṛtam aśnute |
anādi mat-param brahma na sat tat na asat ucyate ||

morph.gloss: to know (jñeya: gerundive 'to be known', acc. sg. neut., object of pravakṣyāmi)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, resuming jñeyam; simply written joined with the following tat, both ending in -t)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut. correlative, an emphatic repetition of yat: 'that which')
to declare, proclaim (pravakṣyāmi: future 1st sg. 'I shall declare')
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, again resuming jñeyam; -t+j-→-j j-)
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known'; jñātvā+amṛtam→jñātvāmṛtam, ā+a→ā)
the deathless, immortality (acc. sg. neut., object of aśnute)
to attain, partake of (aśnute: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains'; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
beginningless (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
me, my (stem form of aham in compounds, first member)
having as one's highest, supreme (mat-param: 'having me as its highest', nom. sg. neut. bahuvrīhi, agreeing with brahma)
brahman, the absolute (kept untranslated per convention; nom. sg. neut., subject of ucyate, in apposition to jñeyam)
being, the existent (sat: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
that, it (tat: nom. sg. neut., resumptive subject; -t+n-→-n n-)
non-being, the non-existent (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to say, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is called'; -t+u-→-d u-)

sentences.l: The-object-of-knowledge which, that I-shall-declare — having-known which one-attains immortality: beginningless, having-me-as-its-highest, brahman — not being; that not non-being is-called.
sentences.i: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless brahman, with me as its highest — it is said to be neither being nor non-being.
sentences.n: This opens the description of brahman that runs, in a series of paradoxes, through verse 17. Jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi doubles the relative and correlative (yat ... tat) purely for emphasis, as already at verse 2's yat taj jñānam, meaning simply 'that which is to be known, I shall declare'. Wikisource prints anādi mat-paraṃ brahma as three separate words; that reading is followed here — anādi, 'beginningless', as an independent adjective, and mat-param as its own bahuvrīhi compound, 'having me [Kṛṣṇa] as its highest' (mat, the compounding stem of aham, + para) — rather than the BORI critical edition's single word anādimat paraṃ brahma, 'possessing no beginning, supreme brahman', where anādimat is instead one adjective (an-ādi + -mat) agreeing with brahma; though no letters differ between the two collated texts, only the word-division, the resulting sense is not quite the same: the vulgate's mat-param names Kṛṣṇa explicitly as brahman's highest object ('having me as its highest'), while BORI's anādimat drops that personal reference and reads simply 'the beginningless, supreme brahman.' Na sat tan nāsad ucyate, 'it is said to be neither being nor non-being', is the first of this chapter's several paradoxical formulas for brahman, continued at verses 13-17. Sandhi: yaj jñātvāmṛtam packs yat+jñātvā (-t+j-→-j j-) and jñātvā+amṛtam (ā+a→ā); tan nāsad ucyate packs tat+na (-t+n-→-n n-), na+asat (a+a→ā), and asat+ucyate (-t+u-→-d u-, voicing before a vowel).

sentences.t:
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
sentences.tr:
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādam tat sarvataḥ akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham |
sarvataḥ śrutimat loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati ||

morph.gloss: foot (pāṇi-pāda: 'hand and foot', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., referring to brahman; simply written joined with the following word)
face (akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham: 'eyes, heads, and faces', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
possessing hearing, having ears (śrutimat: nom. sg. neut., predicate; -t+l-→-l l-)
all, everything (sarvam: acc. sg. neut., object of āvṛtya; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to cover, envelop, pervade (āvṛtya: gerund 'having enveloped')
to stand, exist (tiṣṭhati: present 3rd sg. 'stands, exists')

sentences.l: On-all-sides, hand[s]-and-foot[feet]; it, on-all-sides, eyes-heads-and-faces; on-all-sides, possessing-ears, in-the-world; everything having-enveloped, it-stands.
sentences.i: With hands and feet on every side, eyes, heads, and faces on every side, ears on every side, in this world — it stands enveloping everything.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's series of paradoxical descriptions of brahman, closely echoing — almost quoting — Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.16's sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tat sarvato'kṣiśiromukham | sarvataḥśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati, itself drawing on the Vedic image of a being with organs on every side (cf. Ṛgveda 10.81.3's viśvataś cakṣur uta viśvato mukhaḥ from the Viśvakarman hymn, and the Puruṣa-sūkta's sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt, RV 10.90.1). Sarvataḥ, 'on all sides, everywhere', is repeated three times, building a picture of brahman as somehow possessing every organ everywhere at once, while sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati, 'it stands, having enveloped everything', closes the verse on brahman's all-pervasiveness. Sandhi: tat sarvato'kṣiśiromukham packs tat+sarvataḥ (simply joined, no change before s-), sarvataḥ+akṣi (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha), and akṣi-śiraḥ+mukham (-aḥ+m-→-o, within the compound); śrutimal loke is śrutimat+loke (-t+l-→-l l-, assimilation). Sarvataḥ before śrutimat also shows a visarga retained (unassimilated) before the following ś- (-aḥ+ś-→-aḥ ś-, not the doubled -aś ś- of an assimilating sibilant) — one of two options Pāṇini allows before a sibilant (vā śari, 8.3.36); the same pattern recurs at verse 25's ajānantaḥ śrutvā.

sentences.t:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ।
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsam sarva-indriya-vivarjitam |
asaktam sarva-bhṛt ca eva nirguṇam guṇa-bhoktṛ ca ||

morph.gloss: semblance, appearance (sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsa: 'the semblance of the qualities of all the senses', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
devoid of, free from (vivarjita: past participle, sarva-indriya-vivarjita: 'devoid of all the senses', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
bearer, sustainer (from bhṛ; sarva-bhṛt: 'sustainer of all', nom. sg. neut., predicate; -t+c-→-c c-)
without guṇa, beyond the guṇas (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
enjoyer, experiencer (from bhuj; guṇa-bhoktṛ: 'the enjoyer of the guṇas', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Seeming-to-have-the-qualities-of-all-the-senses, [yet] devoid-of-all-the-senses; unattached, and-indeed sustainer-of-all, without-guṇa, [yet] enjoyer-of-the-guṇas, and.
sentences.i: It appears to have the qualities of every sense, yet is free of every sense-organ; unattached, yet sustaining all; beyond the guṇas, yet the enjoyer of the guṇas.
sentences.n: The paradoxes continue: brahman bears sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsam, 'the semblance of the qualities of all the senses' (it is what makes sensation possible), yet is itself sarva-indriya-vivarjitam, 'devoid of all sense-organs'; it is asaktam, 'unattached', yet sarva-bhṛt, 'the sustainer of all'; nirguṇam, '[itself] without guṇa' — this chapter's first use of guṇa, kept untranslated per convention, referring to the three constituent qualities of nature (sattva, rajas, tamas) that verses 19-23 and chapter 14 treat at length — yet also guṇa-bhoktṛ, 'the enjoyer of the guṇas'. Sandhi: guṇābhāsaṃ is guṇa+ābhāsam (-a+ā-→-ā-); sarvabhṛc caiva packs sarva-bhṛt+ca (-t+c-→-c c-) and ca+eva (a+e→ai).

sentences.t:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥
sentences.tr:
bahiḥ antaḥ ca bhūtānām acaram caram eva ca |
sūkṣmatvāt tat avijñeyam dūra-stham ca antike ca tat ||

morph.gloss: unmoving, motionless (acaram: nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
moving, mobile (caram: nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
subtlety (sūkṣmatvāt: abl. sg. 'because of its subtlety'; written joined with the following tat, both dental -t, no change)
it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+a-→-d a-)
not to be known, incomprehensible (negated gerundive of vi-jñā; nom. sg. neut., predicate)
situated, standing (dūra-stha: 'situated far off, distant', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
near, close by (antike: loc. sg. used adverbially, 'near')
it, that (nom. sg. neut., resumptive subject)

sentences.l: Outside and-inside of-beings, unmoving and-moving too, and; because-of-[its]-subtlety, that [is] incomprehensible; far-off, and-near, and, it.
sentences.i: Outside and inside of all beings, unmoving and yet moving too; because of its subtlety it cannot be known; it is far away, and yet it is near.
sentences.n: The paradoxes continue: brahman is bahiḥ antaḥ ca bhūtānām, 'outside and inside of beings' at once, both acaram, 'unmoving', and caram, 'moving' — encompassing the whole of the unmanifest and manifest creation alike. Sūkṣmatvāt tat avijñeyam, 'because of its subtlety it is incomprehensible', explains why brahman escapes ordinary perception, and the verse closes on dūra-stham ca antike ca tat, 'it is both far and near' — echoing the description of brahman at Īśā Upaniṣad 5, tad dūre tad vantike. Sandhi: bahir antaś ca packs bahiḥ+antaḥ (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-) and antaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṃ packs sūkṣmatvāt+tat (written together, both dental -t, no change) and tat+avijñeyam (-t+a-→-d a-); cāntike is ca+antike (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
sentences.tr:
avibhaktam ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam |
bhūta-bhartṛ ca tat jñeyam grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||

morph.gloss: divided (nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to stand, exist (sthita: past participle 'existing', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
sustainer, supporter (from bhṛ; bhūta-bhartṛ: 'sustainer of beings', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+j-→-j j-)
to know (jñeya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to devour (grasiṣṇu: habitual adjective 'devouring', with -iṣṇu suffix; nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to arise, come forth (prabhaviṣṇu: habitual adjective 'generative, given to arising, bringing forth', with -iṣṇu suffix; nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Undivided, and, among-beings, as-if-divided, and, existing; sustainer-of-beings, and, that [is] to-be-known — devouring, and generative, and.
sentences.i: It exists undivided, and yet seems divided among beings; it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, that which devours them and that which brings them forth.
sentences.n: The paradoxes conclude their run with a final pair: brahman is avibhaktam, 'undivided', in itself, yet appears vibhaktam iva, 'as if divided', when seen distributed among individual beings — the single principle refracted through many bodies, a theme returned to directly at verses 27 and 30-31. Tat jñeyam, 'that is to be known', names it as bhūta-bhartṛ, 'the sustainer of beings', and, in a striking pair of -iṣṇu agent-adjectives (denoting habitual action), grasiṣṇu, 'devouring' (at dissolution), and prabhaviṣṇu, 'generative, bringing forth' (at creation). Sandhi: tajjñeyaṃ is tat+jñeyam (-t+j-→-j j-, as at verse 12's yaj jñātvā and verse 2's yattaj jñānaṃ).

sentences.t:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
sentences.tr:
jyotiṣām api tat jyotiḥ tamasaḥ param ucyate |
jñānam jñeyam jñāna-gamyam hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||

morph.gloss: light, luminary (jyotiṣām: gen. pl. 'of lights'; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+j-→-j j-)
light (jyotiḥ: nom. sg. neut., predicate; -iḥ+t-→-is t-, the visarga assimilating to the dental sibilant before a following dental stop)
darkness (tamasaḥ: abl. sg. 'beyond darkness', with param understood)
beyond, higher than (param: adverbial acc., taken with the ablative tamasaḥ; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to say, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is said')
to know (jñeya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to go, reach (gamya: gerundive 'to be reached', jñāna-gamya: 'to be reached by knowledge', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to stand, be situated (viṣṭhita: past participle 'seated', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-lights even, that [is] the-light; beyond-darkness [it] is-said; knowledge, the-object-of-knowledge, attainable-by-knowledge, in-the-heart of-all, seated.
sentences.i: It is the light even of the lights, said to be beyond darkness; it is knowledge, the object of knowledge, that which is reached by knowledge, seated in the heart of everyone.
sentences.n: The paradoxes give way to a positive climax: brahman is jyotiṣām api tat jyotiḥ, 'the light even of the lights' (sun, moon, fire, and every other luminary), said to be tamasaḥ param, 'beyond darkness' — i.e. beyond ignorance, though tamas here also carries its literal sense, and the pun with the guṇa named at verse 14 is surely intended. It is at once jñānam, 'knowledge', jñeyam, 'the object of knowledge', and jñāna-gamyam, 'that which is reached through knowledge' — subject, object, and goal of knowing all at once — and finally hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam, 'seated in the heart of everyone', closing the description begun at verse 12. Sandhi: tajjyotis tamasaḥ packs tat+jyotiḥ (-t+j-→-j j-) and jyotiḥ+tamasaḥ (-iḥ+t-→-is t-, the visarga assimilating to the dental sibilant before a following dental stop, a new pattern not yet seen this chapter); paramucyate is param+ucyate, simply joined.

sentences.t:
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
iti kṣetram tathā jñānam jñeyam ca uktam samāsataḥ |
mad-bhaktaḥ etat vijñāya mad-bhāvāya upapadyate ||

morph.gloss: the field (nom. sg. neut., subject of uktam)
to know (jñeya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut.)
to say, call (ukta: past participle 'declared', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
me, my (stem form of aham, first member)
devotee (mad-bhakta: 'my devotee', nom. sg. masc., subject; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)
this (etat: acc. sg. neut., object of vijñāya; -t+v-→-d v-)
to understand, comprehend fully (vijñāya: gerund 'having understood')
state, nature, being (mad-bhāva: 'my own state/nature', dat. sg. 'to, toward'; mad-bhāvāya+upapadyate→mad-bhāvāyopapadyate, -a+u-→-o-)
to arrive at, attain (upapadyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains')

sentences.l: Thus the-field, and knowledge, [and] the-object-of-knowledge, [are] declared, in-brief; my-devotee, having-understood this, attains to-my-state-of-being.
sentences.i: Thus the field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge have been declared in brief; my devotee, understanding this, attains to my own state of being.
sentences.n: This closes the chapter's first movement (the field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge, verses 1-17) with a summary and a promise: mad-bhaktaḥ, 'my devotee', who etat vijñāya, 'having understood this', attains mad-bhāvāya, 'to my own state/nature' — echoing 8.5's promise of reaching Kṛṣṇa's own being and anticipating the fuller teaching on nature and the Person that follows from verse 19. Sandhi: coktaṃ is ca+uktam (a+u→o); mad-bhakta etad- shows mad-bhaktaḥ's visarga dropping before the following vowel e-; etad vijñāya is etat+vijñāya (-t+v-→-d v-); mad-bhāvāyopapadyate is mad-bhāvāya+upapadyate (-a+u-→-o-).

sentences.t:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि ।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥
sentences.tr:
prakṛtim puruṣam ca eva viddhi anādī ubhau api |
vikārān ca guṇān ca eva viddhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān ||

morph.gloss: nature (acc. sg. fem., object of viddhi)
the Person (acc. sg. masc., object of viddhi)
beginningless (anādī: dual, agreeing with prakṛtim and puruṣam taken together as a pair)
modification, transformation (vikārān: acc. pl. masc., object of viddhi; -n+c-→-ṃś c-)
the guṇas (guṇān: acc. pl. masc., object of viddhi; -n+c-→-ṃś c-)
arisen, originating (saṃbhava: 'arisen from', prakṛti-saṃbhavān: 'arisen from nature', acc. pl. masc., agreeing with vikārān and guṇān)

sentences.l: Nature [and] the-Person, and-indeed, know [as] both-beginningless, both too; the-modifications and the-guṇas, and-indeed, know [as] arisen-from-nature.
sentences.i: Know that nature and the Person are both beginningless; and know too that the modifications and the guṇas all arise from nature.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's second movement (verses 19-23), the classical Sāṃkhya dualism of prakṛti and puruṣa, both translated throughout this chapter per this pipeline's convention — prakṛti as 'nature' and puruṣa as 'the Person' — rather than left untranslated, consistent with their translation already established at chapters 7-9. Both are declared anādī, 'beginningless' (a dual form covering the pair), while vikārān, 'the modifications' (the twenty-four evolutes catalogued at verses 5-6), and the guṇān, 'the guṇas' (kept untranslated per convention; the three strands sattva, rajas, tamas that compose nature, taken up at length in chapter 14), are said to arise from nature alone — the Person has no part in producing them. Sandhi: viddhy anādī is viddhi+anādī (-i+a-→-y a-); ubhāv api is ubhau+api (-au+a-→-āv a-); vikārāṃś ca and guṇāṃś caiva both show -n+c-→-ṃś c-, the latter compounding further with ca+eva→caiva.

sentences.t:
कार्यकरणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtiḥ ucyate |
puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānām bhoktṛtve hetuḥ ucyate ||

morph.gloss: effect, product, that which is to be produced (gerundive of kṛ, first compound member)
agency, the state of being the agent (kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtva: 'being the agent that produces effects and instruments', loc. sg.)
to say, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is said')
pain (sukha-duḥkha: gen. pl. 'of pleasures and pains')
the state of being the experiencer (from bhoktṛ; loc. sg. 'in being the experiencer')
to say, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: In-being-the-agent-of-effect-and-instrument, [as] cause, nature is-said; the-Person, of-pleasure-and-pain, in-being-the-experiencer, [as] cause is-said.
sentences.i: Nature is said to be the cause in producing effects and instruments; the Person is said to be the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain.
sentences.n: This states the fundamental division of labor between the chapter's two principles: prakṛti is hetuḥ, 'the cause', in kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve, 'in being the agent that produces effects [bodies, objects] and instruments [the senses and organs]' — all activity and production belong to nature — while puruṣa is the cause only bhoktṛtve, 'in being the experiencer' of sukha-duḥkhānām, 'pleasures and pains'; the individual soul does nothing but witness and experience what nature produces, elaborated through verse 23. Wikisource here reads kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve, 'in the being-the-agent of effect and instrument [karaṇa]'; the BORI critical edition instead reads kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve, with long ā in kāraṇa, 'cause' rather than 'instrument' — 'in the being-the-agent of effect and cause' — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint; the vulgate reading, karaṇa, 'instrument', is followed here. Sandhi: prakṛtir ucyate is prakṛtiḥ+ucyate (-iḥ+u-→-ir u-); heturucyate is hetuḥ+ucyate (-uḥ+u-→-ur u-).

sentences.t:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् ।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
sentences.tr:
puruṣaḥ prakṛti-sthaḥ hi bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān |
kāraṇam guṇa-saṅgaḥ asya sat-asat-yoni-janmasu ||

morph.gloss: abiding in, situated in (prakṛti-stha: 'dwelling in nature', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before h-→-o)
to enjoy, experience (bhuṅkte: present middle 3rd sg. 'experiences')
born (from jan; prakṛti-ja: 'born of nature', acc. pl. masc.)
the guṇas (guṇān: acc. pl. masc., object of bhuṅkte)
attachment, contact (guṇa-saṅga: 'attachment to the guṇas', nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
he, his (asya: gen. sg., referring to puruṣa)
good, auspicious (first compound member; sat+asat→sadasat, -t+a-→-d a-)
birth (sat-asat-yoni-janmasu: 'in births in good and evil wombs', loc. pl.)

sentences.l: The-Person, abiding-in-nature, indeed, enjoys the-guṇas-born-of-nature; the-cause [is] his attachment-to-the-guṇas, in-births-in-good-and-evil-wombs.
sentences.i: The Person, dwelling in nature, experiences the guṇas born of nature; attachment to the guṇas is the cause of his birth in good or evil wombs.
sentences.n: This explains how the Person, though inherently a mere witness (verse 20), comes to seem bound: prakṛti-sthaḥ, 'situated/dwelling in nature', he bhuṅkte, 'experiences', the prakṛti-jān guṇān, 'guṇas born of nature' — and this experience becomes guṇa-saṅgaḥ, 'attachment to the guṇas', the kāraṇam, 'cause', of his births sat-asat-yoni-janmasu, 'in wombs good and bad', i.e. in higher or lower forms of rebirth — the cycle of transmigration explained by nothing more than misplaced identification with nature's guṇas. Sandhi: prakṛtistho hi is prakṛti-sthaḥ, -aḥ before h-→-o; guṇasaṅgo'sya is guṇa-saṅgaḥ+asya (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); sadasadyoni- packs sat+asat (-t+a-→-d a-) and asat+yoni (-t+y-→-d y-).

sentences.t:
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः ।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
sentences.tr:
upadraṣṭā anumantā ca bhartā bhoktā mahā-īśvaraḥ |
parama-ātmā iti ca api uktaḥ dehe asmin puruṣaḥ paraḥ ||

morph.gloss: to look on, oversee (upadraṣṭṛ, agent noun 'overseer, witness': upadraṣṭā, nom. sg. masc.; upadraṣṭā+anumantā→upadraṣṭānumantā, ā+a→ā)
to approve, sanction (anumantṛ, agent noun 'approver, one who sanctions': anumantā, nom. sg. masc.)
to bear, sustain (bhartṛ, agent noun 'sustainer': bhartā, nom. sg. masc.)
to enjoy, experience (bhoktṛ, agent noun 'enjoyer, experiencer': bhoktā, nom. sg. masc.)
self (parama-ātman: 'the supreme self', nom. sg. masc.; ātmā+iti→ātmeti, ā+i→e)
to say, call (ukta: past participle 'called', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before d-→-o)
body (dehe: loc. sg. 'in the body'; -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
this (asmin: loc. sg., agreeing with dehe)

sentences.l: The-overseer, the-approver, and, the-sustainer, the-experiencer, the-great-lord; 'the-supreme-self' thus, and-also called — in-this body, the-Person, [is] higher.
sentences.i: The overseer, the approver, the sustainer, the experiencer, the great lord — also called the supreme self — the Person in this body is the higher [reality].
sentences.n: A cascade of epithets for puruṣa in its transcendent aspect (distinct from the merely embodied, guṇa-attached puruṣa of verse 21): upadraṣṭā, 'the overseer/witness'; anumantā, 'the approver, the one who sanctions [nature's activity]'; bhartā, 'the sustainer'; bhoktā, 'the experiencer' (echoing verse 21's bhuṅkte, but now the untainted enjoyer rather than the one bound by attachment); mahā-īśvaraḥ, 'the great lord'; and parama-ātmā, 'the supreme self' — the term used elsewhere in the poem (cf. 6.7's paramātma-samāhitaḥ) for the highest reality present within the individual. Deha ... asmin puruṣaḥ paraḥ, '[this] Person in this body [is] the higher [self]', distinguishes this transcendent puruṣa from the ordinary embodied experiencer just described. Sandhi: upadraṣṭānumantā is upadraṣṭā+anumantā (ā+a→ā); maheśvaraḥ is mahā+īśvaraḥ (ā+ī→e); paramātmeti packs parama+ātmā (a+ā→ā) + ātmā+iti (ā+i→e); cāpyukto packs ca+api (a+a→ā) + api+uktaḥ (-i+u-→-y u-), with uktaḥ's own -aḥ before d-→-o; dehe'smin- is dehe+asmin (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ evam vetti puruṣam prakṛtim ca guṇaiḥ saha |
sarvathā vartamānaḥ api na sa bhūyaḥ abhijāyate ||

morph.gloss: who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)
the Person (acc. sg. masc., object of vetti)
nature (acc. sg. fem., object of vetti)
being, existing, living (vartamāna: present participle, nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
he (nom. sg. masc., the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant)
again, once more (bhūyaḥ: comparative adverb; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
to be born (abhijāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'is born')

sentences.l: Who thus knows the-Person and nature, together-with the-guṇas — in-every-way existing, even — not he again is-born.
sentences.i: One who thus knows the Person and nature, together with the guṇas — however he may be living — is not born again.
sentences.n: The conclusion of this section (verses 19-23): whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti together with the guṇas as fundamentally distinct (the very kṣetra-kṣetrajña discernment named as jñāna at verse 2) is freed from rebirth sarvathā vartamānaḥ api, 'no matter how he is living' — the decisive thing is knowledge, not conduct. Sa, the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant (as already at verse 3), recurs here before bhūyaḥ. Sandhi: vartamāno'pi is vartamānaḥ+api (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); bhūyo'bhijāyate is bhūyaḥ+abhijāyate (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।
अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
sentences.tr:
dhyānena ātmani paśyanti kecit ātmānam ātmanā |
anye sāṃkhyena yogena karma-yogena ca apare ||

morph.gloss: some, a few (kecit: nom. pl. masc.; -t+ā-→-d ā-)
self (ātmānam: acc. sg., object of paśyanti; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
yoga, discipline (karma-yoga: 'the yoga of action', instr. sg.)

sentences.l: By-meditation, in-the-self, some see the-self, by-the-self; others, by-Sāṃkhya, by-yoga; and-yet-others, by-the-yoga-of-action.
sentences.i: By meditation, some see the self in the self, by the self; others by sāṃkhya, by yoga, and yet others by the yoga of action.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's survey of the different paths by which people come to see the distinction taught in this chapter (continued at verse 25): dhyānena, 'by meditation', ātmani ātmānam ātmanā paśyanti, 'they see the self, in the self, by the self' (a triple use of ātman for the seer, the seen, and the instrument of seeing); sāṃkhyena yogena, 'by sāṃkhya, by yoga' (two separate instrumentals, not a compound — cf. l; sāṃkhya kept untranslated per convention, named here as one of the poem's recognized paths, as already at 2.39 and 3.3); and karma-yogena, 'by the yoga of action'. Sandhi: dhyānenātmani is dhyānena+ātmani (-a+ā-→-ā-); kecid ātmānam is kecit+ātmānam (-t+ā-→-d ā-); cāpare is ca+apare (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते ।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
sentences.tr:
anye tu evam ajānantaḥ śrutvā anyebhyaḥ upāsate |
te api ca atitaranti eva mṛtyum śruti-parāyaṇāḥ ||

morph.gloss: not knowing (ajānant: negated present participle, nom. pl. masc.; visarga retained, an alternative to assimilation before the following sibilant ś-)
to hear (śrutvā: gerund 'having heard'; śrutvā+anyebhyaḥ→śrutvānyebhyaḥ, ā+a→ā)
other (anyebhyaḥ: abl. pl. 'from others'; visarga elided before the following vowel u-)
to worship, attend upon (upāsate: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship')
they (te: nom. pl. masc.; -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
to cross over, cross beyond (atitaranti: present 3rd pl. 'they cross'; -i+e-→-y e-)
hearing, what is heard, tradition (first compound member)
intent upon, devoted to (parāyaṇa; śruti-parāyaṇa: 'devoted to what they have heard', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: Others, but, thus not-knowing, having-heard from-others, worship; they too, and, indeed cross-beyond death, devoted-to-what-they-have-heard.
sentences.i: Yet others, not understanding this themselves, worship after hearing it from others; and they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.
sentences.n: This completes the survey of paths with one open to those who cannot follow the preceding methods: anye tu evam ajānantaḥ, 'others, however, not knowing [this] themselves', simply śrutvā anyebhyaḥ upāsate, 'having heard it from others, worship/attend upon [it]' — and even they, śruti-parāyaṇāḥ, 'devoted to what has been heard', atitaranti eva mṛtyum, 'do indeed cross beyond death'. This is the poem's characteristic generosity toward the ordinary believer who cannot manage meditation or philosophical discernment (cf. 12.10-12's descending ladder of practice). Ajānantaḥ is here written with its visarga retained (unassimilated) before the following sibilant ś- of śrutvā — one of two options Pāṇini allows before ś (vā śari, 8.3.36), the same optional pattern already seen at verse 13's sarvataḥ śrutimal loke. (No instance of the assimilated -aḥ+ś-→-aś ś- (doubled, since the visarga converts to match the following ś-) actually occurs in this chapter; the -aḥ+c/ch-→-aś c/ch- seen at verses 3 and 4 is a different, obligatory rule for stops, not sibilants.) Sandhi: tv evam is tu+evam (-u+e-→-v e-); śrutvānyebhya is śrutvā+anyebhyaḥ (ā+a→ā, the resulting form's own visarga then eliding before the following vowel u-); te'pi is te+api (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha); cātitarantyeva packs ca+atitaranti (a+a→ā) + atitaranti+eva (-i+e-→-y e-).

sentences.t:
यावत्संजायते किंचित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥
sentences.tr:
yāvat saṃjāyate kiṃcit sattvam sthāvara-jaṅgamam |
kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogāt tat viddhi bharata-ṛṣabha ||

morph.gloss: to arise, come into being (saṃjāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'arises')
a being, an existent thing (nom. sg. neut., subject)
moving, mobile (sthāvara-jaṅgama: 'stationary or moving', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with sattvam)
the knower of the field (second member)
union, conjunction (kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyoga: 'the union of the field and its knower', abl. sg. 'from')
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of viddhi; -t+v-→-d v-)
Bharata, the Kuru ancestor (first compound member; bharata+ṛṣabha→bharatarṣabha, -a+ṛ-→-ar-)
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative, epithet of Arjuna)

sentences.l: Whatever arises, any being, stationary-or-moving — know that [to arise] from-the-union-of-the-field-and-its-knower, O bull-among-the-Bharatas.
sentences.i: Whatever being comes into existence, stationary or moving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field, Bhārata.
sentences.n: This draws together verses 1-25's whole account into a general statement of cosmology: every sattvam, 'being, creature' — sthāvara-jaṅgamam, 'stationary or moving', i.e. plants as well as animate beings — arises kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogāt, 'from the union/conjunction of the field and its knower', matter joined with consciousness. Bharatarṣabha, 'bull among the Bharatas', is a recurring epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: tad viddhi is tat+viddhi (-t+v-→-d v-); bharatarṣabha is bharata+ṛṣabha (-a+ṛ-→-ar-).

sentences.t:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
samam sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantam parama-īśvaram |
vinaśyatsu avinaśyantam yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||

morph.gloss: equal, the same (acc. sg. masc., predicate)
to stand, abide (tiṣṭhant: present participle, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with parameśvaram)
lord (parama-īśvara: 'the supreme lord', acc. sg. masc., object of paśyati)
perishing (vinaśyat: present participle, loc. pl. 'among things perishing'; -u+a-→-v a-)
not perishing, imperishable (avinaśyant: negated present participle, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with parameśvaram)
he (nom. sg. masc., the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant)

sentences.l: The-same, in-all beings, abiding, the-supreme-lord, not-perishing among-perishing[-things] — who sees [this], he [truly] sees.
sentences.i: The one who sees the supreme lord, abiding equally in all beings, imperishable among things that perish — he truly sees.
sentences.n: A celebrated formula (paśyati ... sa paśyati, 'he sees ... he [really] sees', the repetition itself asserting that ordinary seeing is not seeing at all): parameśvaram, 'the supreme lord', described as samam, 'the same/equal', in every being, tiṣṭhantam, 'abiding', and avinaśyantam vinaśyatsu, 'not perishing among things that perish' — the constant, undivided witness (already named upadraṣṭā at verse 22) present alike in every mortal, changing body. Sandhi: vinaśyatsv avinaśyantaṃ is vinaśyatsu+avinaśyantam (-u+a-→-v a-); sa, the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant (here p-), recurs as at verse 3.

sentences.t:
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् ।
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
samam paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram |
na hinasti ātmanā ātmānam tataḥ yāti parām gatim ||

morph.gloss: equal, the same (acc. sg. masc., predicate)
to see (paśyant: present participle, nom. sg. masc. 'seeing'; simply written joined, the nasal unaffected before h-)
to stand, abide (samavasthita: past participle 'equally situated, abiding equally', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with īśvaram; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
lord (acc. sg. masc., object of paśyan)
to harm, injure (hinasti: present 3rd sg. 'harms'; -i+ā-→-y ā-)
self (ātmanā: instr. sg. 'by the self'; ātmanā+ātmānam→ātmanātmānam, ā+ā→ā)
self (ātmānam: acc. sg., object of hinasti)
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
goal, path (acc. sg. fem., object of yāti)

sentences.l: The-same, seeing, for, everywhere, the-equally-abiding lord — he-does-not harm, by-the-self, the-self; then he-goes to-the-supreme goal.
sentences.i: One who sees the lord abiding equally everywhere does not injure the self by the self; then he goes to the supreme goal.
sentences.n: This draws the ethical conclusion from verse 27's vision: one who sees īśvara, 'the lord', samam, 'equally', everywhere, thereby na hinasti ātmanā ātmānam, 'does not injure the self by the self' — since to harm another being, on this vision, is really to harm the very self one sees present equally in all — and so reaches parāṃ gatim, 'the supreme goal'. The formula ātmanā ātmānam, 'the self by the self', deliberately echoes 6.5's ātmanā ātmānam uddharet, 'let him lift up the self by the self', now specified in its negative, ethical sense. Sandhi: hinasty ātmanātmānaṃ packs hinasti+ātmanā (-i+ā-→-y ā-) and ātmanā+ātmānam (ā+ā→ā); tato is tataḥ, -aḥ before y-→-o.

sentences.t:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः ।
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
prakṛtyā eva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
yaḥ paśyati tathā ātmānam akartāram sa paśyati ||

morph.gloss: action (acc. pl. neut., object of paśyati)
to do, act (kriyamāṇa: present passive participle 'being done', acc. pl. neut., agreeing with karmāṇi)
self (ātmānam: acc. sg., object of paśyati; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
non-doer, not the agent (akartāram: acc. sg. masc., predicate complement of ātmānam)
he (nom. sg. masc., the irregular sandhi form of saḥ before a following consonant)

sentences.l: By-nature alone, and, actions being-done, in-every-way — who sees [this], and likewise the-self as-not-the-agent — he [truly] sees.
sentences.i: One who sees that actions, in every way, are performed by nature alone, and likewise sees the self as not the doer — he truly sees.
sentences.n: This continues the 'sees ... [truly] sees' formula of verse 27, now applied to action: whoever sees that karmāṇi, 'actions', are kriyamāṇāni, 'being performed', prakṛtyā eva, 'by nature alone', sarvaśaḥ, 'in every respect', and correspondingly sees the ātmānam, 'self', as akartāram, 'the non-doer' — restating in this chapter's terms the teaching of 3.27 (prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ) and 5.8-9's insight that the self who truly understands 'does nothing at all'. Sandhi: prakṛtyaiva is prakṛtyā+eva (ā+e→ai); tathātmānam is tathā+ātmānam (ā+ā→ā, with akartāram then simply joined after the -m); sa recurs as at verses 3, 23 and 27.

sentences.t:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
sentences.tr:
yadā bhūta-pṛthak-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśyati |
tataḥ eva ca vistāram brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||

morph.gloss: state, existence (bhūta-pṛthak-bhāva: 'the differentiated existence of beings', acc. sg. neut., object of anupaśyati; simply written joined with the following word, -m unaffected before the vowel)
situated in, abiding in (eka-stha: 'abiding in the One', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bhūta-pṛthak-bhāvam; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
from that, thence (ablative adverb; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)
expansion, diffusion (acc. sg. masc., in apposition with brahma, both governed by saṃpadyate: 'attains the expansion that is brahman' — not a second object of anupaśyati carried from line 1)
brahman, the absolute (kept untranslated per convention; acc. sg. neut., complement of saṃpadyate)
to attain, become (saṃpadyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains, becomes')

sentences.l: When the-differentiated-existence-of-beings, as-abiding-in-the-one, he-sees; then, from-that itself, the-expansion [that-is] brahman he-attains.
sentences.i: When he perceives the differentiated existence of beings as grounded in the One, then, from that very ground, he attains the expanse that is brahman.
sentences.n: This describes the culminating vision in two clauses: bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśyati, 'he sees the differentiated existence of beings as abiding in the One' — the many resting in the single ground — completes line 1. The second line is its own clause with its own verb: tataḥ eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā, 'then, from that very [ground], he attains the expanse that is brahman' — vistāram and brahma are both accusative, in apposition, governed directly by saṃpadyate (which here takes a direct object in the sense 'attains to, reaches', not only a nominative predicate), not a second object of the previous line's anupaśyati. The verse thus moves from seeing multiplicity grounded in unity (line 1) to attaining brahman itself, understood in its aspect as the expansion issuing from that ground (line 2). Sandhi: pṛthagbhāvam is pṛthak+bhāvam (-k+bh-→-g bh-, voicing before a voiced consonant); tata eva is tataḥ+eva, the visarga eliding before the following vowel e-.

sentences.t:
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः ।
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
anāditvāt nirguṇatvāt parama-ātmā ayam avyayaḥ |
śarīra-sthaḥ api kaunteya na karoti na lipyate ||

morph.gloss: the state of being without guṇa (nirguṇatvāt: abl. sg. 'because of')
self (parama-ātman: 'the supreme self', nom. sg. masc., subject)
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., agreeing with paramātmā; paramātmā+ayam→paramātmāyam, ā+a→ā)
imperishable (nom. sg. masc., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
situated in, abiding in (śarīra-stha: 'abiding in the body', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
to smear, taint (lipyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is tainted')

sentences.l: Because-of-[its]-beginninglessness, because-of-[its]-being-without-guṇa, the-supreme-self, this, [is] imperishable; though-abiding-in-the-body, O Kaunteya, it-does-not act, [is] not tainted.
sentences.i: Because it is beginningless and without guṇa, this supreme self is imperishable; though it dwells in the body, Kaunteya, it does not act, and it is not tainted.
sentences.n: This states the transcendent self's untouchedness in causal terms: anāditvāt, 'because of its beginninglessness', and nirguṇatvāt, 'because of its being without guṇa' (not itself composed of the three guṇas that compose nature, as already claimed of brahman at verse 14's nirguṇam), the parama-ātmā, 'supreme self', is avyayaḥ, 'imperishable' — and though śarīra-sthaḥ api, 'though situated in the body', it neither karoti, 'acts', nor is lipyate, 'tainted' — echoing 5.7's yoga-yuktaḥ ... na lipyate and anticipating the two similes (space and sun) of verses 32-33 that explain why. Sandhi: anāditvān nirguṇatvāt packs anāditvāt+nirguṇatvāt (-t+n-→-n n-); paramātmāyam is paramātmā+ayam (ā+a→ā); śarīrastho'pi is śarīra-sthaḥ+api (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yathā sarva-gatam saukṣmyāt ākāśam na upalipyate |
sarvatra avasthitaḥ dehe tathā ātmā na upalipyate ||

morph.gloss: gone [into], pervading (from gam; sarva-gata: 'all-pervading', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
subtlety (saukṣmyāt: abl. sg. 'because of its subtlety'; -t+ā-→-d ā-)
to smear, taint, affect (upalipyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is tainted')
to stand, abide (avasthita: past participle 'situated, abiding', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before d-→-o)
to smear, taint (upalipyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is tainted')

sentences.l: Just-as all-pervading, because-of-[its]-subtlety, space is-not-tainted; everywhere-abiding, in-the-body, likewise the-self is-not-tainted.
sentences.i: Just as space, all-pervading, is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, though present everywhere in the body, is likewise not tainted.
sentences.n: The first of two similes explaining verse 31's claim (continued at verse 33): ākāśam, 'space', though sarva-gatam, 'all-pervading', is na upalipyate, 'not tainted/affected [by what it pervades]', saukṣmyāt, 'because of its subtlety' — and tathā ātmā, 'likewise the self', though sarvatra avasthitaḥ dehe, 'present everywhere in the body', is equally untainted. Sandhi: saukṣmyād ākāśaṃ is saukṣmyāt+ākāśam (-t+ā-→-d ā-); nopalipyate (both occurrences) is na+upalipyate (-a+u-→-o-); sarvatrāvasthito is sarvatra+avasthitaḥ (-a+a-→-ā-), with the participle's own -aḥ before d-→-o; tathātmā is tathā+ātmā (ā+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः ।
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
yathā prakāśayati ekaḥ kṛtsnam lokam imam raviḥ |
kṣetram kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnam prakāśayati bhārata ||

morph.gloss: to illumine, make shine (prakāśayati: causative present 3rd sg. 'illumines'; -i+e-→-y e-)
one, alone (ekaḥ: nom. sg. masc., agreeing with raviḥ)
whole, entire (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with lokam)
the world (lokam: acc. sg., object of prakāśayati; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
this (imam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with lokam)
the field (acc. sg. neut., object of prakāśayati)
the possessor, knower of the field (kṣetrī: nom. sg. masc., subject)
whole, entire (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with kṣetram)

sentences.l: Just-as illumines, alone, the-whole this world, the-sun; the-field, the-knower-of-the-field, likewise, the-whole, illumines, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: Just as the sun alone illumines this whole world, so the knower of the field illumines the whole field, Bhārata.
sentences.n: The second simile, paired with verse 32's space: just as raviḥ, 'the sun', ekaḥ, 'alone', illumines the whole world, so kṣetrī, 'the possessor/knower of the field' (kṣetrin, a synonym here for kṣetrajña, this chapter's central term, coined from kṣetra + the possessive suffix -in), illumines kṛtsnaṃ kṣetram, 'the whole field' — consciousness lighting up the otherwise inert field of matter, exactly as the sun lights up the world it does not itself constitute. Sandhi: prakāśayaty ekaḥ is prakāśayati+ekaḥ (-i+e-→-y e-); lokam imam is simply written joined.

sentences.t:
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
sentences.tr:
kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ evam antaram jñāna-cakṣuṣā |
bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣam ca ye viduḥ yānti te param ||

morph.gloss: the knower of the field (kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ: gen. dual 'of the field and its knower'; -oḥ+e-→-or e-)
the difference, distinction (antaram: acc. sg. neut., object of viduḥ; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
eye (jñāna-cakṣus: 'the eye of knowledge', instr. sg.)
release, liberation (bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣa: 'the liberation of beings from nature', acc. sg. masc., object of viduḥ)
to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present, 'they know'; -uḥ+y-→-ur y-)
the supreme, the highest (acc. sg. neut., object of yānti)

sentences.l: Of-the-field-and-its-knower, thus, the-difference, by-the-eye-of-knowledge, and the-liberation-of-beings-from-nature — who know [this], they go to-the-supreme.
sentences.i: Those who thus know, with the eye of knowledge, the distinction between the field and the knower of the field, and the liberation of beings from nature — they go to the supreme.
sentences.n: The chapter's closing verse gathers its whole teaching into one final promise: those who know, jñāna-cakṣuṣā, 'with the eye of knowledge' (a striking image for insight as a kind of inner seeing, matching the chapter's repeated visual language at verses 27-29's 'sees ... [truly] sees'), the antaram, 'distinction', between kṣetra and kṣetrajña, and bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣam, 'the liberation of beings from nature' (from bondage to nature and its guṇas, the theme of verses 19-23) — such knowers yānti param, 'go to the supreme', closing the chapter on the very promise announced at its outset (verse 2's identification of this knowledge as jñāna itself). Sandhi: kṣetrakṣetrajñayor evam is kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ+evam (-oḥ+e-→-or e-, matching this chapter's recurring dual-genitive pattern first seen at verse 2); vidur yānti is viduḥ+yānti (-uḥ+y-→-ur y-).

glossary.विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि: vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratiḥ jana-saṃsadi — vi-vic — secluded, solitary (vivikta: past participle, first compound member); deśa — place (second member); sevitva — the habit of resorting to, frequenting (vivikta-deśa-sevitva: 'the habit of resorting to secluded places', nom. sg. neut.; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel); a-rati — distaste, disinclination (nom. sg. fem.; -iḥ+j-→-ir j-); jana — people (first compound member); saṃsad — assembly, crowd (jana-saṃsad: 'the assembly of people', loc. sg.)

glossary.तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्: tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam — tattva — the true nature, reality (first compound member); jñāna — knowledge (second member; jñāna+artha→jñānārtha, -a+a-→-ā-); artha — purpose, aim (third member); darśana — seeing, insight (tattva-jñāna-artha-darśana: 'insight into the aim/purpose of the knowledge of reality', nom. sg. neut.)

glossary.पाणिपादं: pāṇi-pādam — pāṇi — hand (first compound member); pāda — foot (pāṇi-pāda: 'hand and foot', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्: tat sarvataḥ akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham — tad — it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., referring to brahman; simply written joined with the following word); sarvatas — everywhere (sarvataḥ: -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); akṣi — eye (first compound member); śiras — head (second member; śiraḥ+mukha→śiromukha, -aḥ before m-→-o); mukha — face (akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham: 'eyes, heads, and faces', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

glossary.तिष्ठति: tiṣṭhati — sthā — to stand, exist (tiṣṭhati: present 3rd sg. 'stands, exists')

glossary.असक्तं: asaktam — a-sakta — unattached (nom. sg. neut., predicate)

glossary.तज्ज्ञेयं: tat jñeyam — tad — it, that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+j-→-j j-); jñā — to know (jñeya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

glossary.ज्योतिषामपि: jyotiṣām api — jyotis — light, luminary (jyotiṣām: gen. pl. 'of lights'; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel); api — even, also

glossary.ज्ञानं: jñānam — jñāna — knowledge (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.ज्ञानगम्यं: jñāna-gamyam — jñāna — knowledge (first compound member); gam — to go, reach (gamya: gerundive 'to be reached', jñāna-gamya: 'to be reached by knowledge', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.विष्ठितम्: viṣṭhitam — vi-sthā — to stand, be situated (viṣṭhita: past participle 'seated', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

glossary.मद्भावायोपपद्यते: mad-bhāvāya upapadyate — mad — me, my (first compound member); bhāva — state, nature, being (mad-bhāva: 'my own state/nature', dat. sg. about: Chapter 13, the Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field (Kṣetrakṣetrajñavibhāgayoga), opens a new movement in the poem with no question from Arjuna at all: Kṛṣṇa simply continues speaking, unprompted, from where chapter 12 left off. He introduces by name the classical Sāṃkhya distinction between the field (kṣetra) — the body together with its whole apparatus of matter, senses, and mental states — and the knower of the field (kṣetrajña), the conscious self that inhabits and knows it, whom Kṛṣṇa identifies with himself, present as such a knower in every field. He analyzes the field into twenty-four constituents (the five elements, the ego, the intellect, the unmanifest, the eleven senses, and the five sense-objects) together with its further modifications, desire, aversion, pleasure and pain among them, and then defines true knowledge not as doctrine but as a long list of virtues — humility, non-violence, equanimity, unwavering devotion, and constancy in self-knowledge — that culminates in a description of brahman built entirely from paradox: it has hands and feet, eyes and faces on every side, yet is without senses; it is unattached yet sustains everything; it is far away and yet near; it is one, undivided, yet seems divided among the many beings it inhabits. The chapter then turns to nature (prakṛti) and the Person (puruṣa), restating their dualism in Sāṃkhya terms — nature alone is the source of all activity and of the three guṇas, while the Person is merely a witness who becomes entangled only through attachment to what he experiences through nature — and surveys the different roads by which this can be understood: meditation, sāṃkhya, the yoga of action, or simple faith taken on the word of others. It closes with two similes, space and the sun, for how the self remains untouched by, even while illuminating, the body it pervades, and with a final teaching that liberation is nothing other than seeing, with the eye of knowledge, this very distinction between the field and its knower.
